claims.sentence: In mathematic, my understanding the solution to the problem is the goal is the new tools and understanding is the goal.
claims.says: In mathematics, as he understands it, solving the problem is not the goal. The new tools and the understanding gained along the way are the goal.
claims.check: This is his view, so it needs no project source. A mathematician has said much the same: William Thurston argues that what mathematicians produce is human understanding, not a quota of theorems or a pile of answers. Quotes opened and read in the paper's text, see source_for_the_idea.
claims.source: Thurston 1994, 'On Proof and Progress in Mathematics', Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 30(2) pp. 161-177, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9404236, Section 1 'What is it that mathematicians accomplish?' and Section 5 'What motivates people to do mathematics?'

claims.sentence: My work create so far help me bring new understanding in machine learning, statisitic into programatic aspect.
claims.says: The project so far has given him new understanding of machine learning and statistics, and of how to turn both into working code.
claims.check: Supported. The smoothness rerun alone uses three statistical tools he coded: replaying each unchanged team three times to measure battle luck, a noise-corrected edit size computed as the square root of the mean squared edit change minus the mean squared replay change, and 95% intervals by bootstrap over starting teams with 2,000 resamples. Whether these were new to him is his to say.

claims.sentence: Able to apply MAP-Elite , reinforcement learning and Cross Entropy method.
claims.says: He was able to apply three methods: MAP-Elites, reinforcement learning and the cross-entropy method.
claims.check: Two of three hold. MAP-Elites: built and run. Deep-surrogate MAP-Elites, after Zhang et al. 2022, was pre-registered 2026-09-30 and run 2026-10-01 over 3 seeds and 6 generations against the existing search loop, and it found stronger teams at that budget. Cross-entropy method: built and run. The cross-entropy loop on the version-3 foundation ran 2026-10-08, with a clean re-run on 2026-10-14 scored on held-out teams. Their win rates come from September and October listed-slot battles, which no longer count, so quote neither number. Reinforcement learning: studied only, never trained. The 2026-08-18 plan was behaviour cloning followed by self-play, and on 2026-10-02 he parked the battle-policy work indefinitely. The policy that plays every battle in the smoothness rerun is VGC-Bench's behaviour-cloning policy, which learns by imitating human replays. That is imitation learning, not reinforcement learning, even though the code calls it the 'behaviour-cloning PPO policy' because it is stored in a reinforcement-learning policy format. His reinforcement-learning work is reading and notes: VGC-Bench's self-play variants and invalid action masking.

source_for_the_idea.verdict: Yes. William Thurston says the product of mathematics is human understanding, not answers or theorems. Quotes below were read in the paper's text, extracted from the arXiv PDF.
source_for_the_idea.author: William P. Thurston
source_for_the_idea.work: On Proof and Progress in Mathematics, Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, Volume 30, Number 2, April 1994, pages 161-177

quotes.text: We are not trying to meet some abstract production quota of definitions, theorems and proofs. The measure of our success is whether what we do enables people to understand and think more clearly and effectively about mathematics.
quotes.section: Section 1, 'What is it that mathematicians accomplish?', page 3

quotes.text: What we are producing is human understanding.
quotes.section: Section 5, 'What motivates people to do mathematics?', last paragraph

quotes.text: They discover by this kind of experience that what they really want is usually not some collection of “answers”—what they want is understanding.
quotes.section: Section 1, 'What is it that mathematicians accomplish?', page 2. The original contains an em dash, so in the post quote one of the two quotes above instead.

source_for_the_idea.fit: Thurston speaks of mathematicians and mathematics, not of a person learning tools through a project. The quote supports Rami's first sentence. It does not say the tools matter more than the answer, only that understanding does.

where_it_fits: It belongs at the close of the post, after the draft's last sentence about building MAP-Elites and the cross-entropy method, because it answers why the work was worth doing once the reader has seen the measurement. Element 11, 'The bigger picture', places smoothness in the series and Rami's reasons, and this paragraph widens that frame from Pokemon to what the project taught him. It is his opinion, so it falls under the 'Admit opinion and perspective' action, but it is not element 15, which weighs other approaches and counter-examples, so it should stand as a short closing paragraph of its own.
